reviews.decision_reason: select_demand admits every corpus row because it uses demand_score >= 3, and the supplied corpus has no record below 3. That brings lower-priority or weakly supported records into the selected data path before normalize truncates them. Under the strict demand criteria, demand_score/keyword-like need text alone is not enough to establish customer demand for all selected records, so this boundary is the localized over-selection point.

normalize receives the selected demand DataFrame, restricts columns, fills neutral sentinels, filters to allowed record identifiers, and returns a bounded one-row index window. The final needs output contains the deterministic top record n06-r01, matching the assigned job output; the row loss here appears intentional from the declared bounded index window rather than the source of the upstream over-selection.

assemble_provenance consumes the normalized one-row needs DataFrame and produces a one-row evidence_sources table with record_id n06-r01, source_id s01, source_weight 5, and rank 1. This matches the assigned job output and provides deterministic ordering over the visible normalized input.
